input.objective:
Deploy one contract, PondGuardDeployer, on Robinhood Chain: its constructor creates PondGuard with CREATE2 at an address whose low 14 bits equal the hook's permission flags, using the bytes32 salt passed as its constructor argument, mined off-chain against the deployer's own address; if the salt cannot be mined in advance, the constructor loops over salts until the computed address carries the flags. The deployer exposes hook() as a view returning the hook's address and does nothing else. PondGuard is a standalone Uniswap v4 hook with no token and no pool of its own; it must be usable by anyone initializing a new pool with it on the PoolManager passed to the deployer as a constructor argument (Robinhood Chain PoolManager 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951).
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. The pool uses a dynamic LP fee that the hook sets per swap between 0.3% and 1.0% based on recent price volatility (the BaseDynamicFee pattern). Expose currentLpFee() as a view.
2. Only pools where one currency is native ETH and the fee tier is 0.3% may be initialized with this hook; any other pool initialization reverts.
3. Take 1.0% of the ETH side of every buy and sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to 0x5Bff2a2FEcD1d6152676813b21346238733bEAB1. Expose claimFees() that anyone may call to redeem claims to the recipient.
No owner functions, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from the pool’s token; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem.
Take the PoolManager as a constructor argument and enable only the callbacks the behavior above needs. Owner, if any, is $owner.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.

facts.label: What each contract does
facts.example: e.g. a vault: deposit ETH, withdraw after a lock

facts.label: Who can call what
facts.assumed: Assumed: an owner who can change settings, and anyone for everything else.
facts.example: e.g. only the owner sets the fee; anyone deposits

facts.label: Numbers the contracts enforce
facts.assumed: The builders will choose limits, ratios and durations and write them in the README. Fee rates and prices they will not choose: name them.
facts.example: e.g. 0.3% fee, 7-day lock, max 10 ETH per wallet

facts.label: Upgrades and pausing
facts.assumed: Assumed: not upgradeable and not pausable.
facts.example: e.g. not upgradeable; owner can pause

facts.label: Outside services and values
facts.example: e.g. Chainlink VRF subscription 1234, or: the owner sets the feed after launch

facts.label: Who receives fees and payouts
facts.assumed: Assumed: the launch's owner, the wallet that pays.
facts.example: e.g. 0x1f9a…c3e2, or: the wallet that pays

facts.label: Minting after launch
facts.assumed: Assumed: a fixed supply that nobody can mint more of.
facts.example: e.g. fixed supply, nobody mints more

facts.label: Transfer rules
facts.assumed: Assumed: plain transfers with no fee or limit.
